correctness.rationale: For the printed \(p=13,n=7\) Table 1 component polynomials, exact division modulo \(169\) gives nonzero remainders \(26+13x+39x^2+117x^4\) from \(x^7-1\) and \(13x^3+13x^4\) from \(x^7+1\), so the literal printed coefficients are not valid \(t=2\) divisors. Exact multiplication-matrix reduction gives ideal cardinalities \(13^9\) and \(13^8\), hence \(13^{17}\) for the direct sum rather than the advertised \(13^8\). The corrected lifts \(\widehat f=(168,6,134,35,163,1)\) and \(\widehat g=(1,29,164,164,29,1)\) divide the two modulus polynomials with cofactors \((1,6,1)\) and \((1,140,1)\), reduce to the printed polynomials mod \(13\), and generate free rank-two components. Fresh exact enumeration reproduces the component weight distribution \(1+1176z^6+27384z^7\); the Gram determinants \(46\) and \(154\) are units modulo \(169\), proving LCD. Thus the corrected direct sum has size \(13^8\), distance \(6\), and meets the Singleton bound.
